summary: vexium-kit fetches and executes remote JavaScript from hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: On invocation of the package's default export, code assembled from concatenated string fragments contacts https://31.97.137.157:45000/icons/116, parses the JSON response, and passes the `credits` field to `new Function(...)` which is then called with `require`, `process`, and `Buffer` bound in — giving the operator of that endpoint arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine with full Node privileges. A companion helper `setDefaultModule` constructs a plausible-looking `cdnjs.<provider>.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/...` URL that is never actually used; the reachable code path assembles the bare-IP endpoint from split string fragments (`protocol` + `separator` + `domain` + `path`). The README advertises the package as a benign utility toolkit, contradicting the fetch-and-eval behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
